levelMapping: SDE II = L61–L62 (≈ Google L4 / Amazon SDE II). L59–60 = SDE I, L63–64 = Senior. In India ~2.5–4.5 YOE lands L61 almost always; L62 typically needs 5–7 YOE (a 4.5-YOE candidate was refused an L62 uplevel in Dec 2025, a 6.5-YOE candidate got L62). A 3.3-YOE backend candidate should expect L61 and confirm the level/job-ID with the recruiter before the loop; downlevelling from Senior to L62 is common.

process.summary: Recruiter call → Codility/HackerRank OA (2 problems, 60–90 min) → a 'virtual loop' of 3–4 one-hour rounds on Microsoft Teams, often all on one day (hiring drives run on Saturdays) or split so that Rounds 1–2 are eliminatory and Rounds 3–4 are scheduled only on good feedback. Typical India SDE II loop: 1–2 DSA rounds (runnable code with tests, 1–2 problems each), one design round (LLD/OOD is at least as common as HLD at L61; rounds labelled 'HLD' frequently turn out to be LLD), a hiring-manager round (project deep dive + behavioral + often a small design/coding/SQL task) and/or an 'As Appropriate' (AA) round with a very senior engineer/manager that mixes behavioral, design and a quick coding question and is the final decision point. Every round opens with 10–15 min on your current project, and interviewers push back on correct answers to test confidence.

rounds.name: Recruiter screen
rounds.what: Why Microsoft, why this role, notice period, preferred language, current work; recruiter maps you to a team/job-ID (WSD/Windows, Azure, M365, Xbox, AI orgs) and explains the round plan.
rounds.probes: Ask which team/product you are interviewing for, how many rounds and whether the design round is HLD or LLD — reports show recruiters often do not volunteer this.

rounds.name: Online assessment
rounds.what: Codility (most common in India) or HackerRank. 2 problems (occasionally 3): one Medium array/string/stack/BFS problem and one Medium-Hard DP/graph/combinatorics problem. Hidden tests run only after the timer ends; pass bar reported between 50% and ~85%. Recruiter-sourced candidates sometimes skip it.
rounds.probes: Reported OA problems: stock buy/sell III variant, base -2 addition of bit arrays, shortest unique substring, Dijkstra+DFS graph, nCr mod p, rotate-prefix-of-string by array, 2D DP story problem, string backtracking, Rotting-Oranges/Walking-Robot-Simulation lookalikes, debug-a-BFS-by-adding-2-lines.

rounds.name: DSA round 1
rounds.what: Intro + 10–15 min on current project, then 1–2 problems in Codility/HackerRank CodePair with screen share. Expected: compilable code, your own test cases, dry run, complexity. Pseudo-code is discouraged. Often two interviewers (one shadowing).
rounds.probes: Trees (validate/recover BST, level-order + zigzag/reverse follow-ups, next-right pointers, LCA/cousins), sliding window (424, 567, 76, 395), linked lists (twin sum, reorder, add numbers), matrix BFS (994, word search), binary-search variants (33). Follow-ups ask you to adapt the same code with minimal change and no extra complexity. Some interviewers add CS fundamentals (hash map/heap internals, OS, C++ STL).

rounds.name: DSA round 2 (or DSA + design)
rounds.what: Second coding round; sometimes replaced by a combined 'DSA + design' hour (e.g. Design Twitter APIs then code the feed, or URL shortener + a sliding-window problem). Story-framed problems are common (LRU cache told as IP-heartbeat management, heap problem told as a scheduling story).
rounds.probes: Priority queues with custom comparators, graph problems (course schedule II variant, weighted grid shortest path, currency-conversion graph, stones-on-graph greedy BFS), data-structure design (max frequency stack as save()/best(), time-based KV store), DP (house robber, word break with Trie).

rounds.name: Design round (LLD/OOD or HLD)
rounds.what: At L61 very often LLD: parking lot, elevator, cache with pluggable eviction, rate limiter, alert system, post-office delivery, Excel sheet, games (snake & ladder, battleship, tic-tac-toe) — explain classes then write working code. HLD when given: URL shortener, telemetry/log metrics, notification system, proximity service, payment service, Google-Docs-like editor, distributed KV store/cache.
rounds.probes: SOLID and which pattern (Strategy/State/Observer) keeps it extensible; thread safety; then for HLD: requirements + capacity, APIs, DB choice/schema, sharding/replication, consistency vs availability, caching, DDoS/rate limiting, multi-region, ID generation. Interviewers change requirements mid-round and expect a redesign.

rounds.name: Hiring manager round
rounds.what: Deep dive into your most complex project (architecture diagram, trade-offs, what you'd do differently, metrics, on-call/incidents), behavioral questions (why switch, conflict, handling work you dislike, pressure), and usually one technical task: idempotent checkout API with pseudocode, SQL vs NoSQL + write SQL queries, parking-system HLD with DB indexing/partitioning, rate limiter LLD→HLD, estimation question (devices in a data centre), a quick coding problem (sort colors, stoi, bishop moves).
rounds.probes: Expects you to defend design decisions under hostile-sounding pushback; data-model and database fundamentals (indexes, partitioning, transactions, unique constraints) come up often; interviewer also sells the team.

rounds.name: As Appropriate (AA) round
rounds.what: Final round with a very senior engineer/manager/director (often 20+ years at MS), scheduled only after positive feedback on the first rounds. Reviews all prior feedback, probes weak spots (a weak design round gets re-tested here), and makes the final hire/no-hire call. Mix: behavioral (growth mindset, failure that hurt the company, mentoring), a design discussion (Google Docs, LinkedIn job search, telemetry) and/or a short coding task (tic-tac-toe playGame, stoi, make-a-machine-sluggish across cores).
rounds.probes: Why Microsoft, how you handle technical disagreement, impact metrics, AI/agents experience (AI-focused teams), OS/C++ internals in Windows/Azure core teams, then your questions about team/location.

process.indiaNotes: Hyderabad, Bengaluru and Noida loops are virtual on Teams and compressed: 3–4 rounds on one day (Saturday hiring drives are common) or 2+2 across a few days; India candidates get rounds 1–2 as an eliminatory pair. L61 is the default band for ≤4.5 YOE; HLD is sometimes replaced by a second LLD/DSA round when experience is judged too light for HLD (reported at 2.4 YOE), and at L61 the design round is LLD more often than HLD. Codility is the usual OA in India (HackerRank in some Noida/Hyderabad drives). Windows (WSD), Azure core and Xbox teams probe OS (processes vs threads, virtual memory, paging) and C++ internals (set/map, STL, memory); other teams are language-agnostic but may ask you to code in your résumé language. Expect to run the code against your own tests, not just pseudo-code. Multiple job-IDs/teams can interview you in parallel with no cooldown; one consolidated offer results. US/EU loops (Redmond, Dublin, Vancouver) look similar but lean more on behavioral-plus-coding rounds, sometimes include a 'research and present a topic' round, and recruiters there are reported as less structured.
process.timeline: Recruiter contact → OA within days; OA result 2 days–2 weeks; loop 1–3 weeks later (hiring events fix the date a month out); rounds 3–4 scheduled 1–7 days after rounds 1–2; verbal result 1–7 days after the last round; written offer 3 days–4 weeks later (tool migrations and job-ID changes caused delays in Dec 2025). Typical end-to-end 3–8 weeks; one Dec 2025 Bengaluru-startup candidate went from recruiter call (24 Nov) to signed offer (24 Dec).
tips: Write compilable code and your own edge-case tests in Codility/CodePair; dry-run before saying done — several offers cite this, several rejections cite 'brute force when the interviewer expected the optimal sliding window'.

Prepare the standard follow-up ladder for tree problems: level order → zigzag → reverse level order with minimal code change; next-right pointers iterative then recursive; validate BST then O(1)-space (Morris) variant.
LRU cache is the single most-reported problem: be ready to make it thread-safe, a singleton, priority/TTL-based, and to refactor eviction into a Strategy interface.

Treat every 'HLD' slot as possibly LLD: clarify scope in the first minute (ask 'HLD first, then LLD if time?'), and keep a class skeleton ready for parking lot, elevator, rate limiter, alert/notification system, cache.

Know several rate-limiting algorithms (token bucket, leaky bucket, fixed/sliding window) with code for token bucket and a Redis sorted-set scale-out story; it appears as LLD, HLD follow-up and HM question.

Have a 20-minute, uninterrupted walkthrough of your hardest project: diagram, DB choice, queues, monitoring, incidents, metrics, what you'd change — it is asked in 2–3 of the 4 rounds and decided at least two reported rejections.
Expect deliberate pushback on correct answers (heapify complexity, idempotency design); hold your position calmly and explain why, but ask for clarification before trying to 'prove' something.
Revise OS and language internals if the team is Windows/Azure core/C++: processes vs threads, virtual memory, paging, deadlocks, how std::set/map keep order, hash map/heap complexities.
Database fundamentals show up in HM rounds: SQL vs NoSQL, when NoSQL fits, adding a column to a huge table, indexing/partitioning, transactions, writing a top-N query.

Behavioral themes are growth mindset, handling disagreement/conflict, a failure that affected the company, why switch, and 'why Microsoft'; prepare STAR stories with metrics, and one about AI/agents if the team is AI-focused.
Follow up with HR if the process stalls — candidates report rounds being rescheduled 1–3 times and a closed position reopening with another team two months later using the same feedback.
process.notes: OA platform is Codility (India default) or HackerRank; the live coding tool is Codility/HackerRank CodePair over Teams with screen share. No formal 'bar raiser'; the AA interviewer plays that role and can override a single No-Hire. Generally all interviewers must give Hire. The loop is language-agnostic (C#, C++, Java, Python all seen) but a Java-heavy résumé may be asked to code in Java, and C++ teams ask C++-specific follow-ups. One Windows team ran an AI-assisted LLD round where the candidate was allowed to use an LLM and was judged on prompt quality and evaluation of the output; AI-focused orgs reportedly pilot Copilot-enabled coding, and the AA interviewer in one loop compared the candidate's tic-tac-toe code with ChatGPT output. Microsoft's careers site allows AI for preparation but not during assessments unless explicitly permitted. No cooldown between parallel team processes; rejected candidates have re-interviewed within months with a different panel. LLD/OOD rounds exist for this band, so the 'lld' section is populated. Other problems seen in 2024 loops/OAs but trimmed from the list: Add Two Numbers (trailing carry), Merge k Sorted Lists, Cheapest Flights Within K Stops (modified), Merge In Between Linked Lists, Largest Number, Restore IP Addresses, Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock III (OA), negabinary addition (OA), repair a broken circular doubly linked list, Bus Routes/Word Ladder II (2025 list).

dsa.title: LRU Cache
dsa.variant: Often story-framed (IP addresses that expire when heartbeats stop; 'implementation-heavy' narrative). Follow-ups reported: make it thread-safe, make the class a singleton and justify it, extend to a priority-based cache, add TTL/expiry, refactor eviction into a pluggable Strategy interface, add dependency management via topological sort, explain inheritance vs composition.
dsa.evidence: Reported in at least 8 loops: Dec 2025 L62 WSD (thread-safe + singleton), Dec 2025 India reject (IP heartbeat variant), 2026 L61/62 (LRU + topo-sort dependencies), Hyderabad Azure 2024 (priority-cache follow-up), Nov 2025 Noida R1 story version, 2025 consolidated list, Dec 2025 SSE design round, 2024 Azure SDE-2 distributed-cache coding round

dsa.title: Permutation in String
dsa.variant: Interviewer expects the fixed-size sliding window immediately; a candidate who generated permutations (O(n!)) was marked down and later rejected.
dsa.evidence: Dec 2025 India SDE-2 Round 1; also #37 in the July-2026 tag snapshot

dsa.title: Longest Repeating Character Replacement
dsa.variant: Asked as 'a variation' in a Windows-team DSA round (discuss brute force then optimal) and verbatim in a Nov 2025 hiring drive where the candidate needed hints to reach the variable window.
dsa.evidence: 2 reports: 2026 Windows SDE-2 R1, Nov 2025 hiring drive R1

dsa.title: Minimum Window Substring
dsa.variant: Both strings limited to 26 lowercase letters; follow-ups: state complexity, optimize, then clean up the code (Noida L61 R1, rated Strong Hire).

dsa.title: Longest Substring with At Least K Repeating Characters
dsa.variant: Asked as a variation in a Hyderabad L61 DSA round (two interviewers, Codility, runnable code required).

dsa.title: Longest Substring with At Most K Distinct Characters
dsa.variant: Also appears as the follow-up to Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters (LC 3), which itself was asked in a 2025 DevOps SWE round and the 2025 consolidated list.
dsa.evidence: Hyderabad SDE-2 R1 (LC 340); LC 3 in Jun 2025 SWE DevOps R1 and 2025 consolidated list; IGotAnOffer commonly-asked list

dsa.title: Rotting Oranges
dsa.variant: Multi-source BFS; appears both in Codility OAs (lookalike) and as the warm-up in a Noida L61 DSA round followed by two BST problems.
dsa.evidence: Aug 2025 Noida L61 R1; May 2025 Hyderabad OA lookalike; #16 in tag snapshot

dsa.title: Validate Binary Search Tree
dsa.variant: One Azure SQL screen insisted on an O(1) extra-space solution (Morris inorder traversal) after the standard inorder approach; usually paired with Recover BST.
dsa.evidence: Aug 2025 Noida L61 R1; Jan 2025 Blind Azure SQL screen; IGotAnOffer list

dsa.title: Recover Binary Search Tree
dsa.variant: Phrased as 'find the two swapped/incorrectly placed nodes'; brute force first then O(n) inorder with prev pointer.
dsa.evidence: Aug 2025 Noida L61 R1; Hyderabad SDE-1 R2

dsa.title: Binary Tree Level Order Traversal with zigzag and reverse follow-ups
dsa.variant: Level order (LC 102) → zigzag (LC 103) → reverse level order (LC 107); each follow-up must be a minimal edit of the same code without raising time/space complexity. Also asked as 'build the tree from input then print level order' and zigzag alone (2025 consolidated list, Hyderabad Azure 2019).
dsa.evidence: May 2025 Hyderabad L61 R3; 2024 SDE-II R2; 2025 consolidated list

dsa.title: Populating Next Right Pointers in Each Node II
dsa.variant: Asked as 'given a node return its next node on the same level' and as 'connect nodes at the same level'; solve iteratively then the interviewer asks for recursive (Hyderabad L62). Easier LC 116 version (complete tree) in a Mar 2024 L61 screen.
dsa.evidence: Blind 2025 downlevel loop R1; Hyderabad L62 offer; Mar 2024 L61 R1; GfG Hyderabad SDE-2

dsa.title: Two Sum IV – Input is a BST
dsa.variant: Candidate's inorder-to-array + two pointers (O(n) space) was accepted only partially; interviewer wanted forward and reverse BST iterators for O(h) space.

dsa.title: Lowest Common Ancestor of a Binary Tree / Deepest Leaves
dsa.variant: LC 236 asked after the train-platform problem (Noida L61, Oct 2024); LC 1123 (LCA of deepest leaves) asked in Hyderabad SDE-2 R1.
dsa.evidence: Noida L61 R1 (Oct 2024); Hyderabad SDE-2 R1

dsa.title: Cousins in Binary Tree (find all cousins of a node)
dsa.variant: Asked as 'return all cousins of a given node' (same depth, different parent): brute force with complexity, then optimized single BFS.

dsa.title: Maximum Width of Binary Tree
dsa.variant: Full program incl. test harness had to be written and run; index-labelling (2i, 2i+1) approach expected after a naive attempt failed.

dsa.title: Maximum Twin Sum of a Linked List (no modification allowed)
dsa.variant: Constraint: list must not be modified (no reversing the second half); expected two pointers plus an n/2 array or stack.

dsa.title: Reorder List (L1,L2,…,R1,R2,… → L1,R1,L2,R2,…)
dsa.variant: Interleave the first half with the second half in order (not reversed, unlike LC 143); O(n²) was accepted as a warm-up.

dsa.title: Linked list cycle: detect, find length, break the cycle
dsa.variant: Three-part follow-up chain: detect (LC 141), length of loop, then remove the loop by finding the node before the cycle start.

dsa.title: Asteroid Collision
dsa.variant: Asked as a close variant; 20 minutes incl. tests. Stack problems generally are a Microsoft OA staple ('medium stack problem' in the Dec 2025 OA).
dsa.evidence: 2024 SDE2 R1; Dec 2025 OA stack problem

dsa.title: Sort Colors (Dutch National Flag)
dsa.variant: Asked in the engineering-manager round; correct three-pointer solution but interviewer wanted it coded faster.

dsa.title: Search in Rotated Sorted Array
dsa.variant: Paired with grid word search in one hour (Dec 2025). 'Modified binary search on an array, not on LeetCode' also reported in a Redmond hiring-event round; simple binary search in a Hyderabad L62 R1.
dsa.evidence: Dec 2025 R2; Aug 2025 Redmond loop; Dec 2025 Hyderabad R1

dsa.title: Word Search (grid)
dsa.variant: Horizontal/vertical moves only; candidate used BFS from every matching start cell. Also in the IGotAnOffer common list.

dsa.title: Count Subarrays With Fixed Bounds
dsa.variant: Asked alongside a grid-reachability-within-time-T problem before two design rounds.

dsa.title: Decrypt String from Alphabet to Integer Mapping
dsa.variant: Warm-up before a max-subarray-with-length-≤k problem in a hiring-drive round that also covered OAuth/JWT/Docker.

dsa.title: Maximum subarray sum with length at most k
dsa.statement: You are given profits[] where positive entries are profit months and negative entries are loss months. Return the maximum sum of any contiguous subarray whose length is at most k. Expected approach: prefix sums with a monotonic deque of minimum prefix over the last k positions (O(n)), or Kadane adapted with a window bound. The candidate could not finish it even with hints.
dsa.variant: A plain 'variant of maximum subarray' was also asked in the Hyderabad L62 offer loop.
dsa.evidence: Nov 2025 SDE-2 hiring drive R2; Hyderabad L62 R1

dsa.title: Most-frequent-then-most-recent data structure (save/best)
dsa.statement: Design a structure with save(num) and best(): best() returns and removes the value with the highest frequency, breaking ties by the most recently saved number. Example: saving 2,5,8,2,8,9,2 then calling best() four times yields 2, 8, 2, 9. This is LC 895 Maximum Frequency Stack in disguise (map of freq → stack of values plus value → freq map).
dsa.variant: Candidate solved with doubly linked list + hash maps, then realised maps alone suffice. Also listed as 'Maximum Frequency Stack' in the 2025 consolidated list.
dsa.evidence: Nov 2025 Noida L61 R1; 2025 consolidated list

dsa.title: Time Based Key-Value Store
dsa.variant: Paired with a digit-string partition problem; interviewer disliked the vector+binary-search answer's redundant checks — write it cleanly.

dsa.title: Minimum partitions of a digit string into dictionary words (Trie)
dsa.statement: Given a string of digits and a word list (may contain duplicates), split the string into the fewest substrings such that every piece is in the list; return the minimum count. Recursion is the obvious start; the interviewer wanted a Trie-guided DP (Word Break II / minimum-cut style).
dsa.variant: Word Break family; Word Ladder II also listed in the 2025 consolidated list.

dsa.title: Meeting Rooms II / Minimum platforms
dsa.variant: Asked as 'minimum number of train platforms' (Noida L61, with corner cases + complexity) and as a 'variation of minimum meeting rooms' with a follow-up the candidate could not debug live (2026 L61/62).
dsa.evidence: 2026 SDE 2 L61/62 DSA round; Oct 2024 Noida L61 R1

dsa.title: Priority queue with custom sort order (story problem)
dsa.statement: Heap problems are repeatedly dressed as scheduling/story prompts: build a priority queue of structs with a multi-key custom comparator, then process items in that order (e.g. tasks by priority then arrival, or 'sorting + priority queue' variations). Expected: clean struct, comparator, heap operations and complexity.
dsa.variant: Dec 2025 Hyderabad R2 ('priority queue problem with custom sort order'); Dec 2025 L62 R2 ('sorting and priority queue variation'); Nov 2025 Noida R2 (story-based heap problem).

dsa.title: Course Schedule II (topological sort) with a variant follow-up
dsa.variant: Full HackerRank solution with all tests, then a variant explained in pseudocode; topological sort also appeared as 'LRU cache that manages dependencies via topo sort' in a 2026 LLD round.

dsa.title: Shortest path in a weighted grid with constraints
dsa.statement: Find the minimum-cost path from one cell of a weighted grid to another subject to extra constraints (blocked cells, limited moves/time). Variants reported: Dijkstra on a grid (Bengaluru 2026 R1), and 'can you reach bottom-right from top-left within time T with blocked cells' (Dec 2025).
dsa.variant: Clean code and edge cases were emphasised over just a working answer.
dsa.evidence: 2026 Bengaluru SDE II R1; Dec 2025 SSE loop

dsa.title: Currency conversion as a weighted graph
dsa.statement: Given exchange rates between currency pairs, answer conversion queries (or find how much value is retained converting A→B through intermediates). Model rates as weighted edges and DFS/BFS multiplying weights along the path — the EU Azure candidate did not recognise it as a graph problem until hinted.
dsa.variant: Equivalent to LC 399 Evaluate Division.

dsa.title: Balance stones on a connected graph (adjacent difference ≤ 1)
dsa.statement: Each node of a connected undirected graph holds some stones. You may only add stones. Return the minimum total stones to add so that every pair of adjacent nodes differs by at most one. Reported approach: process nodes from a max-heap by current stones, BFS outward and greedily raise each neighbour to (current − 1) when it is lower.

dsa.title: All paths from a source with a target sum (graph backtracking)
dsa.statement: Given an undirected graph that may contain cycles, a source vertex and a target sum, enumerate all simple paths starting at the source whose node (or edge) weights add up to the target. Needs a visited set per path and pruning; the interviewer pushed many counter-questions and ended on complexity.
dsa.variant: Preceded by Longest Common Prefix (LC 14) as a warm-up in the same hour.

dsa.title: Longest Common Prefix
dsa.variant: Warm-up before a graph problem; #6 in the tag snapshot.

dsa.title: Simplify Path
dsa.variant: Asked as a similar file-path normalisation problem, followed by a Two Sum variant with extra constraints rated medium-hard.

dsa.title: Design Twitter (code the feed)
dsa.variant: Given as a 1.5-hour 'DSA + system design' round: postTweet/getNewsFeed/follow/unfollow, millions of users, thread safety; interviewer pushed to improve time/space from 'store all tweets + heap' to capping each user's stored tweets at n, then code and test.

dsa.title: Find Median from Data Stream (salaries) + concurrency follow-up
dsa.variant: Insert salaries into a stream and report the median after each insert; follow-ups on complexity, then how multiple threads inserting concurrently are handled (locks/critical sections).

dsa.title: Binary array neighbour-equality iterations (state after n steps)
dsa.statement: A binary array evolves each step: a cell becomes 1 if its two neighbours are equal, else 0 (ends treated as 0). Return the array after n steps where n can be huge. Discuss naive simulation, then detect the period of the state sequence (hash states) and jump n mod period; handle first/last index edge cases. Essentially LC 957 Prison Cells After N Days generalised.

dsa.title: House Robber (max sum of non-adjacent elements)
dsa.variant: Asked as maxSumSubsequence([3,2,5,10,7]); paired with implementing a stack with an array (push/pop/peek).

dsa.title: Fixed-size queue backed by an array / stack using array
dsa.variant: Implement enqueue/dequeue with head/tail pointers over a fixed array (Blind 2025 loop); implement stack push/pop/peek on an array (Nov 2024 L61). Microsoft frequently asks 'implement a data structure from scratch and outline tests'.
dsa.evidence: Blind 2025 downlevel loop R3; Nov 2024 L61 R1; Glassdoor Toronto loop ('implement a queue')

dsa.title: String to Integer (stoi) with edge cases
dsa.variant: Asked in the AA / hiring-manager round as a quick coding check in C++; focus on whitespace, sign, overflow, invalid characters.

dsa.title: Bishop moves on an 8x8 chessboard
dsa.statement: Given a bishop's (x, y) on a standard chessboard, print every square it can reach in one move. Expected clean code: iterate four diagonal directions with a direction array in one loop and stop at the board edge, rather than four separate while loops.
dsa.variant: Asked by a senior engineering manager after a project deep dive.

dsa.title: Tic-tac-toe: implement playGame
dsa.variant: AA round with a senior AI leader: write a working game loop with win detection, then compare your code with ChatGPT's output and discuss the differences.

dsa.title: Make a machine run sluggishly (multi-core CPU saturation)
dsa.statement: Write code whose execution noticeably slows down a machine. The expected answer is not an infinite loop on one thread but spawning one busy thread/process per core (and optionally memory pressure) so CPU utilisation hits 100% across all cores; discuss how the OS schedules threads. The inverse ('parallelise a task across an 8-core CPU') was asked in a 2024 HM round.
dsa.variant: AA round problem-solving/debugging mindset question.
dsa.evidence: Aug 2025 Noida L61 AA; 2024 Azure SDE-2 HM round

dsa.title: Implement the Linux cp command
dsa.statement: Write cp: open the source, create/truncate the destination, copy in buffered chunks, preserve permissions, handle directories/recursion, symlinks, partial writes and errors. Follow-ups went into syscalls, buffering, file descriptors and C++ RAII — a Windows/core-OS team question.

dsa.title: Shortest unique substring (OA)
dsa.statement: Given a string S, return the length of the shortest substring that occurs exactly once in S. Count occurrences of substrings by increasing length (or use suffix structures) and return the first length that has a unique one. Appears repeatedly in Microsoft Codility OAs.
dsa.variant: Paired with 'maximise distinct two-digit combinations in a digit string' (De Bruijn flavour) in a Nov 2024 OA; also in a Hyderabad SDE-1 Codility OA.
dsa.evidence: Nov 2024 SDE-2 (Data) OA; SDE-1 Hyderabad OA

dsa.title: Rotate prefix characters by array values (OA)
dsa.statement: Given string s and integer array arr (len ≤ len(s)), for each i rotate every character in s[0..i] forward by arr[i] letters (backward if negative) with wrap-around. Return the final string; e.g. s='abcd', arr=[1,-2,3,0] → 'ccfd'. Efficient solution: suffix sums of arr give each position's total shift in O(n).
dsa.variant: HackerRank OA, 90 min, 2 problems; the other was a medium sliding-window problem.

dsa.title: nCr modulo prime and Dijkstra+DFS graph (OA)
dsa.statement: HackerRank OA pair: (1) a graph problem needing Dijkstra plus a DFS over the resulting structure; (2) compute C(n, k) mod p for large inputs using factorials and modular inverses (Fermat). Candidate completed problem 1 and ~80% of problem 2 and still advanced.
dsa.evidence: Aug 2025 Noida L61 OA (two write-ups of the same loop)
